questions.q: Two stars of masses $m$ and $2m$ at a distance $d$ rotate about their common centre of mass in free space. The period of revolution is
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
$F = \dfrac{G \left(2m\right)m}{d2} = \left($2m\right){ω}^{2}\left($d / 3\right)$

\dfrac{Gm}{d2} = {ω}^{2}\dfrac{d}{3}

$⇒ {ω}^{2} = $\dfrac{3Gm}{d3}

$⇒ $\omega = \sqrt{\dfrac{3Gm}{d3}}

$⇒ T = $\dfrac{2\pi}{ω} ==2\pi\sqrt{\dfrac{d3}{3Gm}}$

$

questions.q: Assuming the earth to be a sphere of uniform mass density, the weight of a body at a depth $d = \dfrac{R}{2}$ from the surface of earth, if its weight on the surface of earth is $200N$, will be : (Given $R =$ radius of earth)
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The acceleration due to gravity with depth is&

$g^{'} = g \left($1 - $\dfrac{d}{R}\right)

The given data is~

$W = 200Nd = $\dfrac{R}{2}

Let the weight be at the given depth,~$W '$. Hence, the value is~

$mg^{'} = mg \left(1 - \dfrac{\dfrac{R}{2}}{R}\right) = m\left(\dfrac{g}{2}\right)$

The Weight~$W '$~$= \dfrac{W}{2} = \dfrac{200}{2} = 100N$

$

questions.q: The escape velocity of a body on a planet $A$~is $12kms^{- 1}$. The escape velocity of the body on another planet $B$, whose density is four times and radius is half of the planet $A$, is&
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
We know that escape velocity is given by,

$v = \sqrt{\dfrac{2GM}{R}} ⇒ \dfrac{vA}{vB} = \sqrt{\dfrac{MA}{MB} \times \dfrac{RB}{RA}} = \sqrt{\dfrac{{ρ}_{A}{RA}^{3}}{{ρ}_{B}{RB}^{3}} \times \dfrac{RB}{RA}} = \sqrt{\dfrac{{ρ}_{A}{RA}^{2}}{{ρ}_{B}{RB}^{2}}} = \sqrt{\dfrac{1}{4} \times \dfrac{4}{1}} ⇒ {v}_{B} = {v}_{A} = 12kms^{- 1}$

questions.q: For a body projected at an angle with the horizontal from the ground, choose the correct statement
options: Gravitational potential energy is maximum at the highest point.
The horizontal component of velocity is zero at highest point.
The vertical component of momentum is maximum at the highest point.
The kinetic energy (K.E.) is zero at the highest point of projectile motion.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
In a projectile motion, a particle has two components of velocity. The horizontal component of velocity remains constant over time, while the vertical component of velocity changes.

At highest point, the vertical component of velocity& \left({v}_{y}\right)$~becomes zero, but the horizontal component is non-zero. So the kinetic energy of the particle is not zero.

The formula to calculate the potential energy \left(U\right)$~of the particle is given by

$U = mgh . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ( 1 )$

where,~$m$~is the mass,~$g$~is the acceleration due to gravity and~$h$& is the vertical height attained by the object.

Hence, the potential energy is maximum when the projectile attains the maximum height.

questions.q: Two planets $A$~and $B$ of equal mass are having their period of revolutions ${T}_{A}$ and ${T}_{B}$ such that ${T}_{A} = 2{T}_{B}$. These planets are revolving in the circular orbits of radii ${r}_{A}$ and ${r}_{B}$ respectively. Which out of the following would be the correct relationship of their orbits?
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
From& Kepler's law of periods,

$T^{2} ∝ R^{3}$

Therefore,

$⇒ \left(\dfrac{TA}{TB}\right)2 = \left(\dfrac{rA}{rB}\right)3$

$⇒ {2}^{2} = {r}_A^{3}{r}_B^{3}$,~$⇒ {r}_A^{3} = 4{r}_B^{3}$

questions.q: A planet takes $200$ days to complete one revolution around the Sun. If the distance of the planet from Sun is reduced to one fourth of the original distance, how many days will it take to complete one revolution?
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The Law of Periods: The square of the period of any planet is proportional to the cube of the semimajor axis of its orbit.

$T^{2} ∝ r^{3}$

Therefore, we can write

${T}_{1}^{2}{r}_{1}^{3} = {T}_{2}^{2}{r}_{2}^{3}$

$⇒ \dfrac{( 200{)}^{2}}{r3} = {T}_{2}^{2}\left(\dfrac{r}{4}\right)3$

$⇒ \dfrac{200 \times 200}{4 \times 4 \times 4} = {T}_{2}^{2}$

$⇒ {T}_{2} = 25$ days

questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Given here,& $m = 100kg$

Gravitational force,~${F}_{AP} = \dfrac{Gm^{2}}{\left(13\sqrt{2}\right)2}$,

${F}_{BP} = \dfrac{Gm^{2}}{\left(13\right)2}$~and~${F}_{CP} = \dfrac{Gm^{2}}{\left(13\sqrt{2}\right)2}$

Net gravitational force,~

${F}_{net} = {F}_{BP} + {F}_{AP}\cos 45 ° + {F}_{CP}\cos 45 °$

~$= \dfrac{G × {10}^{4}}{132} \left($1 + $\dfrac{1}{2}\right)

$F ≃ 100G$

$

questions.q: If the radius of earth shrinks by $2 %$ while its mass remains same. The acceleration due to gravity on the earth's surface will approximately
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The acceleration due to gravity on the surface of the earth is given by,& $g = \dfrac{GM}{R2}$.

The radius shrunk by~$2 %$. Therefore,~$\dfrac{∆ R}{R} \times 100 = - 2 %$.

As the mass is constant and the change in the radius of the earth is relatively small, we can write

$\dfrac{∆ g}{g} = - 2\dfrac{∆ R}{R} ⇒ \dfrac{∆ g}{g} \times 100 = 4 %$

Hence, the acceleration due to gravity increases by~$4 %$.

questions.q: A satellite of mass $\frac{M}{2}$ is revolving around earth in a circular orbit at a height of $\frac{R}{3}$ from earth surface. The angular momentum of the satellite is $M \sqrt{\frac{G M R}{x}}$. The value of $x$ is ______ , where $M$ and $R$ are the mass and radius of earth, respectively. ( G is the gravitational constant)
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
$\begin{aligned} & \text { orbital velocity } v_0=\sqrt{\frac{\mathrm{GM}}{4 \mathrm{R} / 3}}=\sqrt{\frac{3 \mathrm{GM}}{4 \mathrm{R}}} \\ & \text { Angular momentum of satellite }=\frac{\mathrm{M}}{2} \mathrm{v}_0 \frac{4 R}{3} \\ & =\frac{M}{2} \cdot \sqrt{\frac{3 \mathrm{GM}}{4 \mathrm{R}}} \cdot \frac{4 \mathrm{R}}{3} \\ & =M \sqrt{\frac{\mathrm{GMR}}{3}} \\ & x=3\end{aligned}$ (ii) Since mass of satellite is comparable to the mass of earth.
$\begin{aligned} & \frac{\text { G.M. } \frac{\mathrm{M}}{2}}{\left(\frac{4 \mathrm{R}}{3}\right)^2}=\frac{\mathrm{M}}{2} \omega^2 \cdot \frac{8 \mathrm{R}}{9} \\ & \omega=\sqrt{\frac{81 \mathrm{GM}}{128 \mathrm{R}^3}}\end{aligned}$ Angular momentum of satellite about common centre of mass, $\begin{aligned} & L=\frac{M}{2} \cdot\left(\frac{8 R}{9}\right)^2 \cdot \omega \\ & L=M \sqrt{\operatorname{GMR}\left(\frac{8}{81}\right)} \\ & x=\frac{81}{8} \simeq 10 \end{aligned}$

questions.q:
If the acceleration due to gravity experienced by a point mass at a height $h$~above the surface of earth is same as that of the acceleration due to gravity at a depth $\alphah \left(h ≪ {R}_{e}\right)$ ) from the earth surface. The value of \alpha will be _____ .

(use~${R}_{e} = 6400km)

$
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Acceleration due to gravity at a height $h$~above the earth's surface is given by~$g \left($1 - $\dfrac{2h}{Re}\right)~

And~acceleration due to gravity at depth $d$ below the earth surface is given by~$g \left(1 - \dfrac{d}{Re}\right)$.

As~${g}_{above} = {g}_{below}$

So,~$g \left(1 - \dfrac{2h}{Re}\right) =g \left($1 - $\dfrac{d}{Re}\right)

$⇒ $\dfrac{2h}{Re} = \dfrac{d}{Re}

$⇒ \alphah = d$

Thus, the value of~\alpha =$2.

$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
$L =$ constant;~$L = I\omega$

From the conservation of angular momentum,

$\dfrac{2}{5}MR^{2}{ω}_{1} = \dfrac{2}{5}M\left(\dfrac{R}{4}\right)2{ω}_{2} ⇒ MR^{2}{ω}_{1} = \dfrac{MR^{2}{ω}_{2}}{16} ⇒ \dfrac{\omega1}{\omega2} = \dfrac{1}{16}$

Using~$\omega = \dfrac{2\pi}{T}$~for each case along with the respective angular frequencies,

$\dfrac{T2}{T1} = \dfrac{1}{16}$

$⇒ \dfrac{T1}{T2} = \dfrac{16}{1}$

Using~${T}_{1} = 24h,x = 16$& by comparing with the given time period in the question.

questions.q: Three identical spheres of mass m , are placed at the vertices of an equilateral triangle of length a. When released, they interact only through gravitational force and collide after a time $\mathrm{T}=4$ seconds. If the sides of the triangle are increased to length 2 a and also the masses of the spheres are made 2 m , then they will collide after _____ seconds.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
$\begin{aligned} & \mathrm{T} \propto \mathrmm^{\mathrm{x}} \mathrmG^{\mathrm{y}} \mathrma^{\mathrm{z}} \\ & \mathrm{T} \propto \mathrmM^{\mathrm{x}}\left[\mathrmM^{-1} \mathrm{~L}^3 \mathrm{~T}^{-2}\right]^y[\mathrm{~L}]^{\mathrm{z}} \\ & \mathrm{T} \propto \mathrmM^{\mathrm{x}-\mathrm{y}} \mathrmL^{3 \mathrm{y}+\mathrm{z}} \mathrmT^{-2 \mathrm{y}} \\ & \mathrm{x}-\mathrm{y}=0 \Rightarrow \mathrm{x}=\mathrm{y} \\ & -2 \mathrm{y}=1 \Rightarrow \mathrm{y}=-\frac{1}{2}, \mathrm{x}=-\frac{1}{2} \\ & \Rightarrow 3 \mathrm{y}+\mathrm{z}=0 \\ & \mathrm{z}=-3 \mathrm{y}=\frac{3}{2}\end{aligned}$
Hence
$\begin{aligned}
& \mathrm{T} \propto \mathrm{~m}^{-1 / 2} \mathrmG^{-1 / 2} \mathrma^{3 / 2} \\ & \mathrm{~T} \propto\left(\frac{\mathrm{a}^3}{\mathrm{~m}}\right)^{1 / 2} \\ & \mathrm{~T}=4 \times\left(\frac{2^3}{2}\right)^{1 / 2}=8 \mathrm{~s}
\end{aligned}$
